title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 244 (Right to apply under section 241)

content.overview: Section 244 fixes who may apply to the Tribunal under section 241. In the case of a company having a share capital, the application may be made by not less than one hundred members or not less than one-tenth of the total number of members, whichever is less, or by any member or members holding not less than one-tenth of the issued share capital of the company. In the case of a company not having a share capital, the application may be made by not less than one-fifth of the total number of members. The Tribunal may, on an application, waive all or any of the requirements specified in this section so as to enable the members to apply under section 241.
content.glance: s. 241 standing: share-capital co — ≥100 members or ≥1/10 of members (whichever less), or members holding ≥1/10 of issued share capital; no share capital — ≥1/5 of members; Tribunal may waive.
content.study: The following members of a company shall have the right to apply under section 241, namely: (a) in the case of a company having a share capital, not less than one hundred members of the company or not less than one-tenth of the total number of its members, whichever is less, or any member or members holding not less than one-tenth of the issued share capital of the company, provided that the applicant or applicants have paid all calls and other sums due on their shares; (b) in the case of a company not having a share capital, not less than one-fifth of the total number of its members. The Tribunal may, on an application made to it in this behalf, waive all or any of the requirements specified in this section so as to enable the members to apply under section 241. Current-law framing: confirm company type (share capital or not); compute numerical or capital threshold; check calls paid where capital threshold is used; seek waiver if below threshold. Class-action standing under s. 245 has its own prescribed thresholds and is distinct.

sections.heading: Share-Capital Company
sections.body: Not less than 100 members or not less than one-tenth of total members, whichever is less; or any member(s) holding not less than one-tenth of issued share capital (calls and other sums due must be paid).

sections.heading: Company Without Share Capital
sections.body: Not less than one-fifth of the total number of members.

sections.heading: Waiver
sections.body: Tribunal may waive all or any of the requirements so as to enable members to apply under s. 241.

sections.heading: Relationship to Class Action
sections.body: Standing for s. 241 is fixed here. Class-action standing under s. 245 is separate and prescribed by rules.

examples.title: Capital threshold
examples.body: Three members together hold 12% of issued share capital and have paid all calls. They have standing under s. 244 to apply under s. 241 without needing 100 members.

examples.title: Waiver
examples.body: A single minority member holds 3% and seeks to apply under s. 241. The Tribunal may, on application, waive the numerical and capital requirements under s. 244.

hypotheticals.question: Can one member with 2% of capital always apply under s. 241?
hypotheticals.analysis: Not as of right. Section 244 requires either the numerical threshold or not less than one-tenth of issued share capital. Below that, the member must obtain a Tribunal waiver under s. 244.

distinctions.title: Right to apply (s. 244) vs application for relief (s. 241)
distinctions.left: Who may apply — numerical and capital thresholds; waiver

misconceptions.trap: Any single shareholder can always file under s. 241 without more.
misconceptions.correction: Section 244 imposes numerical or capital thresholds. Below threshold, the applicant must obtain a Tribunal waiver.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 244 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm company type. II. Compute numerical or capital threshold. III. Check calls paid if capital path. IV. Seek waiver if needed. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Membership facts; threshold calculation; waiver if sought; precise relief.

examTips: 100 or 1/10 members (whichever less), or 1/10 issued capital.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: State the standing thresholds under s. 244.
enhancement.definition: Section 244 prescribes the numerical and share-capital thresholds for members to apply under section 241, and empowers the Tribunal to waive those requirements.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Oppression and mismanagement applications require a minimum collective stake so that the Tribunal is not flooded by isolated grievances, subject to a fairness waiver.
essentialIngredients: Share-capital co: ≥100 or ≥1/10 members (whichever less), or ≥1/10 issued capital with calls paid
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 244 is the standing gate for s. 241 applications.
enhancement.problemApplication: Compute threshold; apply or seek waiver.

verification.note: Section-text level; case-law verification separate; no new citations invented.
